source.title: Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions

Locators are journal pages (journal page = pdf page + 766).

arXiv 1512.02683v3 (24 January 2017), SHA-256 76bb3576bc75dc1c5214597197e3d8ef62abc10784e2b2625657a0e7ea1821ff: the two versions carry the same 112 numbered statements, and every recorded misprint was compared with it.

summary:
Yun and Zhang prove the first higher-derivative Gross–Zagier formula: every Taylor coefficient of an automorphic L-function, not only the first, is an intersection number. Let X be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over F_q (p > 2), ν : X′ → X an étale double cover with X′ geometrically connected, G = PGL_2 and T = (Res_{F′/F}G_m)/G_m the associated nonsplit torus. For r even and an everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representation π of G(A), Theorem 1.2 reads

  (1/(2(log q)^r|ω_X|))·ℒ^{(r)}(π_{F′}, 1/2) = ([Sht^μ_T]_π, [Sht^μ_T]_π)_π,

where ℒ(π_{F′}, s) = ε(π_{F′}, s)^{−1/2}L(π_{F′}, s)/L(π, Ad, 1) is self-dual under s ↦ 1−s, and [Sht^μ_T]_π is the π-component of the Heegner–Drinfeld cycle θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T] — the class of the moduli of T-shtukas with r legs, a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack of dimension r, inside the moduli Sht′^r_G of PGL_2-shtukas with r legs on X′, of dimension 2r. For r = 0 it is Waldspurger's formula (Remark 1.3) and for r = 1 the Gross–Zagier formula; Theorem 1.6 is the same identity in ℓ-adic cohomology, Theorem 1.7 deduces that the intersection pairing is positive definite on the cuspidal part, and Theorem 1.8 is a Kronecker limit formula for the Eisenstein part, ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩ = 2^{r+2}(log q)^{−r}L^{(r)}(η, 0).

The proof compares two relative trace formulae and is global throughout — no local orbital integrals are matched (Remark 1.10).
- **Analytic side (§§2–4).** The regularized distribution J(f, s) = ∫^{reg}_{[A]×[A]}K_f(h_1, h_2)|h_1h_2|^sη(h_2) is a Laurent polynomial in q^s (Propositions 2.1, 2.3); it has an orbital expansion over u = inv(γ) ∈ P¹(F) ∖ {1}, computed explicitly for f = 1_K (Proposition 2.4), and, after killing the Eisenstein part with the Eisenstein ideal (Theorem 4.3), a spectral expansion J(f, s) = (1/2|ω_X|)Σ_π ℒ(π_{F′}, s+1/2)λ_π(f) — Waldspurger's formula via Jacquet's relative trace formula (Proposition 4.5, Theorem 4.7).
- **Geometric side (§§5–7).** The Hecke action on Sht^r_G is defined by cycles on the whole stack rather than by étale correspondences away from bad points (Proposition 5.10), so I_r(f) = ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], f ∗ θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩ makes sense; it is rewritten, through the Octahedron Lemma, as a trace on a Hitchin-type moduli stack M_d (Theorems 6.5–6.6); and a finiteness analysis of the H-action on H^{2r}_c(Sht_G) makes the image of the Hecke algebra a finitely generated algebra of Krull dimension one, giving an orthogonal spectral decomposition (Theorems 7.14, 7.16).
- **Comparison (§§3, 8–9).** Both sides become traces of Frobenius on direct images over the same base: Rf_{M,*}Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i,j}K_i ⊠ K_j with the Hecke correspondence acting by (d−2j) (Propositions 8.2–8.3), and Rf_{N_d,*}L_d ≅ K_{d_{11}} ⊠ K_{d_{12}} as a middle extension (Proposition 8.5). This gives (log q)^{−r}J_r(u, h_D) = I_r(u, h_D) for every orbit and every divisor of large degree (Theorem 8.1), hence for all f ∈ H by a density argument (Theorem 9.2).

Appendix A develops the intersection theory this needs on Deligne–Mumford stacks locally of finite type: Chow groups of proper cycles, a corrected filtration on K′_0 defined through finite flat presentations, the compatibility of refined Gysin maps with derived pullback (Proposition A.5), the **Octahedron Lemma** (Theorem A.10) allowing intersections to be taken in any order, and a Lefschetz trace formula for the intersection with the graph of Frobenius (Proposition A.12). Appendix B proves the **super-positivity** Λ^{(r)}(π, 1/2) ≥ 0 for self-dual cuspidal π of GL_n under the Riemann hypothesis — unconditional over function fields — which is what makes Theorem 1.7 unconditional.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (the higher Gross–Zagier/Waldspurger formula: cycle-theoretic form)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over k = F_q (p > 2), ν : X′ → X an étale double cover with X′ geometrically connected, G = PGL_2, and r an even integer. For an everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representation π of G(A) with coefficient field E_π, let [Sht^μ_T]_π ∈ W_π be the projection of the Heegner–Drinfeld cycle θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T] to the π-eigenspace of W. Then, in E_π, (1/(2(log q)^r|ω_X|))·ℒ^{(r)}(π_{F′}, 1/2) = ([Sht^μ_T]_π, [Sht^μ_T]_π)_π, where ℒ(π_{F′}, s) = ε(π_{F′}, s)^{−1/2}L(π_{F′}, s)/L(π, Ad, 1) satisfies ℒ(π_{F′}, s) = ℒ(π_{F′}, 1−s) and |ω_X| = q^{−deg ω_X}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 772; proof completed in §9.3.2, p. 879, published version
items.note: Remark 1.3: for r = 0 this is exactly Waldspurger's formula for an everywhere unramified π, (1/2|ω_X|)ℒ(π_{F′}, 1/2) = |∫_{T(F)\T(A)}φ(t)dt|²/⟨φ, φ⟩_Pet. Remark 1.4 compares the E_π-valued pairing with the Néron–Tate height with coefficients of Yuan–Zhang–Zhang. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (the same formula in ℓ-adic cohomology)
items.statement: With V′ = H^{2r}_c((Sht′^r_G) ⊗_k k̄, Q_ℓ)(r) and λ a place of E_π above ℓ, let [Sht^μ_T]_{π,λ} ∈ V′_{π,λ} be the projection of the cycle class cl(θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]) under the decomposition (1.7). Then (1/(2(log q)^r|ω_X|))·ℒ^{(r)}(π_{F′}, 1/2) = ([Sht^μ_T]_{π,λ}, [Sht^μ_T]_{π,λ})_{π,λ} in E_{π,λ}; in particular the right-hand side lies in E_π.
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p. 774; proof completed in §9.2, pp. 878–879, published version

items.name: Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.5 = 7.16 (spectral decompositions of the cycle and cohomology modules)
items.statement: Theorem 1.1: the quotient W = W̃/W̃_0 of the H-module generated by the Heegner–Drinfeld cycle by the kernel of the intersection pairing decomposes orthogonally as W = W_Eis ⊕ (⊕_π W_π), π running over the finitely many everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representations, with each W_π an E_π-vector space of dimension at most one. Theorem 1.5 (made precise in Theorem 7.16): V′_{Q_ℓ} = V′_{Q_ℓ,Eis} ⊕ (⊕_m V′_{Q_ℓ,m}) orthogonally, m running over a finite set of maximal ideals of H_{Q_ℓ} with finite residue fields E_m, each summand finite dimensional and supported at m; the pairings lift to E_m-bilinear pairings.
items.locator: Theorems 1.1 and 1.5, pp. 772–773; proof of 1.1 in §9.3.1, p. 879; Theorem 7.16, pp. 867–868, published version
items.note: Unlike (1.5), the m occurring in (1.7) are not known to be automorphic. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Theorem 1.7 (positivity of the intersection pairing on the cuspidal part)
items.statement: The restriction of the intersection pairing (·,·) to the orthogonal complement W_cusp of W_Eis in W is positive definite. The proof uses that E_π is totally real (the Hecke operators are self-adjoint for the Petersson product), Theorem 1.2 for each real embedding, L(π_ι, Ad, 1) > 0, and the super-positivity ℒ^{(r)}(π_{ι,F′}, 1/2) ≥ 0 of Theorem B.2.
items.locator: Theorem 1.7 and proof, pp. 774–775, published version
items.note: Evidence for the Hodge standard conjecture for a subquotient of the Chow group of middle-dimensional cycles on Sht′^r_G. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Theorem 1.8 (a Kronecker limit formula: the Eisenstein part of the self-intersection)
items.statement: For r > 0 even, ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩_{Sht′^r_G} = (2^{r+2}/(log q)^r)·L^{(r)}(η, 0), where L(η, s) is the complete L-function of the quadratic idele class character η = η_{F′/F}. Remark 1.9: odd-order derivatives would need the analogous spaces for odd r.
items.locator: Theorem 1.8 and Remark 1.9, p. 775; proof in §9.1.1, pp. 874–876; the r = 0 case in Remark 9.3, pp. 876–877, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §1.7 (the two relative trace formulae and the key identity (1.9))
items.statement: The proof compares an analytic relative trace formula for J(f, s) = ∫^{reg}_{[A]×[A]}K_f(h_1, h_2)|h_1h_2|^sη(h_2)dh_1dh_2 (A the diagonal torus of G) with a geometric one for I_r(f) = ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], f ∗ θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩_{Sht′^r_G}: both have an orbital expansion indexed by u ∈ P¹(F) ∖ {1} and a spectral expansion, and the theorem follows from the key identity (1.9) I_r(f) = (log q)^{−r}J_r(f) for all f ∈ H, where J_r(f) = (d/ds)^r|_{s=0}J(f, s). Remark 1.10: the proof of (1.9) is entirely global — no local orbital-integral comparison — and in fact gives the term-by-term identity of the orbital expansions.
items.locator: §1.7, (1.8)–(1.9), Remark 1.10, pp. 775–778, published version
items.note: The r = 0 case of the analytic RTF is Jacquet's reproof of Waldspurger's formula; the r = 1 case was considered by Zhang. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §2.1–2.2 (the automorphic kernel, the weighted orbital integrals and the regularized J(f, s))
items.statement: For f ∈ H one forms the kernel K_f(h_1, h_2) = Σ_{γ ∈ G(F)}f(h_1^{−1}γh_2) and, for (n_1, n_2) ∈ Z², the truncated integrals J_{n_1,n_2}(f, s) over the components of [A] × [A] of given degrees, weighted by |h_1h_2|^sη(h_2); the invariant of an orbit is inv(γ) ∈ P¹(F) ∖ {1}, giving the orbital pieces J_{n_1,n_2}(γ, f, s) and J(γ, f, s) = Σ_{(n_1,n_2)}J_{n_1,n_2}(γ, f, s), and J(u, f, s) for u = inv(γ).
items.note: Routed to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 as a source.

items.name: Propositions 2.1, 2.3 and Lemma 2.2 (finiteness and the definition of J(f, s))
items.statement: Proposition 2.1: J_{n_1,n_2}(f, s) vanishes when |n_1| + |n_2| is large, so J(f, s) := Σ_{(n_1,n_2) ∈ Z²}J_{n_1,n_2}(f, s) is defined and is a Laurent polynomial in q^s. Lemma 2.2: the sum defining K_{f,γ} has finitely many nonzero terms, since for all but finitely many u ∈ P¹(F) ∖ {0, 1, ∞} the kernel vanishes identically on A(A) × A(A). Proposition 2.3: for every γ ∈ G(F) the integral J_{n_1,n_2}(γ, f, s) vanishes for |n_1| + |n_2| large, treated separately for regular semisimple and non-regular-semisimple orbits.
items.locator: Propositions 2.1 and 2.3, Lemma 2.2, §§2.3–2.5, pp. 783–787, published version
items.note: Routed to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.4 and Corollary 2.5 (the orbital integrals for f = 1_K, and J_r(1_K))
items.statement: For f = 1_K: J(u, 1_K, s) = L(η, 2s) + L(η, −2s) for u ∈ {0, ∞}, = 1 for u ∈ k ∖ {0, 1}, and 0 otherwise. Hence J_r(1_K) = 4L(η, 0) + q − 2 = 4·#Jac_{X′}(k)/#Jac_X(k) + q − 2 for r = 0; = 2^{r+2}(d/ds)^r|_{s=0}L(η, s) for r > 0 even; and 0 for r > 0 odd.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4 and Corollary 2.5, pp. 787–788, published version
items.note: Corollary 2.5 is the analytic input for the Kronecker limit formula, Theorem 1.8. Routed to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 as a source.

items.name: §3.1–3.3 (the moduli N_d, the local systems L_d and Proposition 3.1)
items.statement: For d = (d_{11}, d_{12}, d_{21}, d_{22}) ∈ Σ_d (quadruples of non-negative integers with d_{11} + d_{22} = d = d_{12} + d_{21}), N_d is a moduli space of pairs of effective divisors with a section, mapping to the base A_d = X̂_d ×_{Pic^d_X} X̂_d. Proposition 3.1: the morphism d is an open embedding and N_d is a geometrically connected k-scheme; for d ≥ 2g′ − 1 = 4g − 3 it is smooth of dimension 2d − g + 1; and there is a commutative diagram exhibiting f_{N_d} : N_d → A_d as proper. Each N_d carries a rank one local system L_d coming from the double cover X′/X.
items.locator: §§3.1–3.3, Proposition 3.1, pp. 788–793, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Proposition 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 (orbital integrals as Frobenius traces)
items.statement: For an effective divisor D on X of degree d and the Hecke function h_D: if u is not in the image of inv_D then J(γ, h_D, s) = 0 for every γ with inv(γ) = u; if u = inv_D(a) with a ∈ A_D(k) = Γ(X, O_X(D)) and u ∉ {0, 1, ∞}, then J(γ(u), h_D, s) = Σ_{d ∈ Σ_d}q^{(2d_{12}−d)s}Tr(Frob_a, (Rf_{N_d,*}L_d)_a). Corollary 3.3: consequently J_r(u, h_D) = (log q)^rΣ_{d ∈ Σ_d}(2d_{12} − d)^rTr(Frob_a, (Rf_{N_d,*}L_d)_a) when u = inv_D(a), and 0 otherwise.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2 and Corollary 3.3, pp. 793–797, published version
items.note: This is the analytic side turned into a sheaf-theoretic trace, in the style of the geometric proofs of fundamental lemmas (Ngô, Yun). items.name: §4.1 (the Eisenstein ideal) and Lemma 4.2
items.statement: The Eisenstein ideal I_Eis ⊆ H is the kernel of the map a_Eis : H → Q[Pic_X(k)]^{ι_Pic} through which H acts on the Eisenstein spectrum (Definition 4.1). Lemma 4.2: for every x ∈ |X| the ring Q[Pic_X(k)]^{ι_Pic} is a finitely generated H_x-module, and a_Eis is surjective, so Spec(a_Eis) is a closed embedding.
items.locator: §4.1, Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2, pp. 797–799, published version
items.note: Routed to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.3 and Lemma 4.4 (the kernel and J(f, s) for f in the Eisenstein ideal)
items.statement: Theorem 4.3: for f ∈ I_Eis the automorphic kernel decomposes as K_f = K_{f,cusp} + K_{f,sp} (the Eisenstein contribution is annihilated). Lemma 4.4: consequently J(f, s) = Σ_π J_π(f, s), the sum over everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representations of G(A).
items.locator: Theorem 4.3 and Lemma 4.4, pp. 800–803, published version
items.note: Routed to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.5, Lemma 4.6 and Theorem 4.7 (the spectral expansion: Waldspurger's formula)
items.statement: Proposition 4.5: for an everywhere unramified cuspidal π with Hecke character λ_π, J_π(f, s) = (1/2|ω_X|)ℒ(π_{F′}, s + 1/2)λ_π(f); the proof computes the product of the two toric periods P(φ, s)P_η(φ, s) against the Petersson norm, whence the adjoint L-value in the normalization of ℒ. Lemma 4.6 records the change of the local Whittaker/zeta normalization under a change of additive character. Theorem 4.7: for f ∈ I_Eis, J(f, s) = (1/2|ω_X|)Σ_π ℒ(π_{F′}, s + 1/2)λ_π(f), an identity in E[q^{−s}, q^s].
items.locator: Proposition 4.5, Lemma 4.6, Theorem 4.7, pp. 803–807, published version
items.note: This is Waldspurger's formula in the everywhere unramified function-field case, obtained from Jacquet's relative trace formula. Routed to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 as a source.

items.name: §5.1–5.2 (Hecke stacks, moduli of rank n shtukas and Sht^r_G)
items.statement: For a sign vector μ ∈ {±}^r satisfying the balance condition, Hk^μ_n classifies chains of rank n bundles with elementary modifications of the prescribed types at the legs; Remark 5.2: (p_0, p_X) : Hk^μ_n → Bun_n × X^r is representable, proper and smooth of relative dimension r(n−1) with iterated P^{n−1}-bundle fibres. Definition 5.3 defines Sht^μ_n as the fibre product of Hk^μ_n with the graph of Frobenius. Theorem 5.4 (Drinfeld for r = 2, Varshavsky in general): Sht^μ_n is a Deligne–Mumford stack locally of finite type and π^μ_n : Sht^μ_n → X^r is separated and smooth of relative dimension r(n−1). Lemmas 5.5–5.6 give canonical isomorphisms Hk^μ_G ≅ Hk^{μ′}_G for different μ and the Cartesian description of Sht^μ_G, so that Sht^r_G is independent of μ; Corollary 5.7 transfers Theorem 5.4 to G = PGL_2.
items.locator: §§5.1–5.2, Definition 5.3, Remark 5.2, Theorem 5.4, Lemmas 5.5–5.6, Corollary 5.7, pp. 807–811, published version
items.note: GS.1 plans global Hecke stacks and GS.2 multi-leg shtuka stacks with their representability and smoothness for a general reductive G; PGL_2 and GL_n are instances.

items.name: §5.3 (Hecke correspondences on Sht^r_G and their action on Chow groups)
items.statement: For an effective divisor D, Sht^r_G(h_D) is the moduli of shtukas with an extra modification of degree D, giving a self-correspondence (←p, →p) of Sht^r_G. Lemma 5.8: ←p, →p and (←p, →p) are representable and proper; Lemma 5.9: the geometric fibres of Sht^r_G(h_D) → X^r have dimension r (proved in §6.4.4), so dim Sht^r_G(h_D) = 2r and the fundamental cycle pushes forward to cCh_{2r}(Sht^r_G × Sht^r_G)_Q. Proposition 5.10: h_D ↦ H(h_D) is a ring homomorphism H → cCh_{2r}(Sht^r_G × Sht^r_G)_Q. Remark 5.11 compares this with the traditional correspondence Γ(g) defined only away from the bad points. Lemma 5.12: the action of any f ∈ H on Ch_{c,*}(Sht^r_G)_Q and Ch_{c,*}(Sht′^r_G)_Q is self-adjoint for the intersection pairing.
items.locator: §5.3, Lemmas 5.8–5.9, Proposition 5.10, Remark 5.11, Lemma 5.12, pp. 811–814, published version
items.note: Defining the Hecke action by cycles on the whole of Sht^r_G, rather than by étale correspondences away from bad points, is what allows intersection numbers over all of X^r. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §5.4–5.5 (the torus shtukas Sht^μ_T, the Heegner–Drinfeld cycle and I_r(f))
items.statement: For the nonsplit torus T = (Res_{F′/F}G_m)/G_m, Sht^μ_T is the moduli of T-shtukas with legs on X′; Lemma 5.13: π^μ_T : Sht^μ_T → X′^r is a torsor under the finite groupoid Pic_{X′}(k)/Pic_X(k), hence finite étale, so Sht^μ_T is a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack of pure dimension r. The finite morphism θ^μ : Sht^μ_T → Sht′^r_G := Sht^r_G ×_{X^r}X′^r gives the Heegner–Drinfeld cycle θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T] ∈ Ch_{c,r}(Sht′^r_G)_Q, and I_r(f) := ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], f ∗ θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩_{Sht′^r_G}. Lemma 5.16: I_r(f) does not depend on the choice of μ.
items.locator: §§5.4–5.5, Lemma 5.13, Lemma 5.16, pp. 814–821, published version

items.name: §6.1–6.2 (the moduli M_d, the map f_M, and the Hecke self-correspondence H)
items.statement: Proposition 6.1: the moduli stack M_d (of a rank two bundle with a line subbundle and extra data) is a proper Deligne–Mumford stack, smooth of pure dimension 2d − g + 1 for d ≥ 2g′ − 1, with a proper map f_M : M_d → A_d and ν̂_d : X̂′_d → X̂_d proper, fitting into a Cartesian diagram. Lemma 6.2: the Hecke stack Hk^μ_{M,d}, as a self-correspondence of M_d, is the r-fold composition of a single correspondence H. Lemma 6.3: over the open locus A♦_d there is a natural map H♦ → I′_d to the incidence scheme. Lemma 6.4: γ_0 : Hk^μ_{M♦,d} → M♦_d is finite surjective, so dim Hk^μ_{M♦,d} = dim M♦_d = 2d − g + 1, and the image of the complement in M_d × M_d has dimension at most d + 2g − 2.
items.locator: §§6.1–6.2, Proposition 6.1, Lemmas 6.2–6.4, pp. 821–827, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Theorem 6.5 and Theorem 6.6 (the intersection number as a trace, and as a Gysin intersection)
items.statement: Theorem 6.5: for an effective divisor D of degree d ≥ max{2g′ − 1, 2g}, I_r(h_D) = Σ_{a ∈ A_D(k)}Tr((f_{M,!}[H♦])^r_a ∘ Frob_a, (Rf_{M,!}Q_ℓ)_a). Theorem 6.6: there is a class ζ ∈ Ch_{2d−g+1}(Hk^μ_{M,d})_Q restricting to the fundamental cycle over Hk^μ_{M,d}|_{A♥_d ∩ A♦_d} with I_r(h_D) = ⟨ζ, Γ(Fr_{M_d})⟩_D, the local intersection number with the graph of Frobenius in the sense of §A.4.5. Lemma 6.7 shows that for d ≥ 3g − 2 the endomorphism f_{M,!}cl(ζ♥) of Rf_{M,!}Q_ℓ|_{A♥_d} is independent of the choice of such a class.
items.locator: Theorems 6.5–6.6, Lemma 6.7, pp. 828–830; proof of 6.6 in §6.3.6, pp. 839–840, published version
items.note: This is the most technical part of the paper: the intersection of the Heegner–Drinfeld cycle with its Hecke translate is rewritten, through the Octahedron Lemma, as a Lefschetz-type trace on a Hitchin-like moduli stack. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §6.3–6.4 (the auxiliary moduli stacks and the verification of the intersection-theoretic hypotheses)
items.statement: Lemma 6.8: ←p, →p : H_d → Bun_G are representable and smooth of pure relative dimension 2d, so H_d is smooth of pure dimension 2d + 3g − 3, and M♥_d ↪ M_d is the open preimage of A♥_d. Lemma 6.9 identifies Hk^μ_{M♥,d} with the preimage of A♥_d. Lemma 6.10 computes the dimensions of Hk^{r,◦}_{G,d} and of the fibres of s : Hk^r_{G,d} → X_d × X^r. Lemma 6.11: for d ≥ max{2g′ − 1, 2g} the diagram (6.26) satisfies the conditions of §A.2.8, so the refined Gysin map (Π^μ × Π^μ)^! is defined and ζ♥ = (Π^μ × Π^μ)^![Hk′^r_{G,d}] restricts to the fundamental cycle. Lemma 6.12 decomposes Sht^r_{G,d} and Sht′^r_{G,d} over the k-points of X_d; Corollary 6.13 identifies Sht^μ_{M♥,d}; Lemma 6.14: the diagram (6.31) satisfies the conditions of §A.2.10 and (id, Fr_{H_d})^![Hk′^r_{G,d}] = [Sht′^r_{G,d}], which also proves Lemma 5.9; Lemma 6.15 computes dim H′ = d + r through the affine Schubert variety Gr_{1^r,d}.
items.locator: §§6.3–6.4, Lemmas 6.8–6.15, Corollary 6.13, pp. 830–845, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §7.1 (the Hecke action on the cohomology of Sht_G: Proposition 7.1, Lemmas 7.2–7.3)
items.statement: Proposition 7.1: h_D ↦ C(h_D) is a ring homomorphism H → End(H^i_c(Sht_G ⊗_k k̄)) for every i. Lemma 7.2: this action is self-adjoint for the cup product pairing. Lemma 7.3: the cycle class map cl is H-equivariant in every degree, so the cycle-theoretic and cohomological Hecke modules match.
items.locator: §7.1, Proposition 7.1, Lemmas 7.2–7.3, pp. 845–849, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §7.2–7.3 (the stratification by instability and the cohomological constant term)
items.statement: Sht_G is exhausted by the open substacks Sht^{≤d}_G indexed by functions d ∈ D recording the instability of the chain. Lemma 7.4: for d ∈ D_+ the map p_d : Sht^d_B → Sht_G induces an isomorphism onto Sht^d_G. Lemma 7.5: if d(i) > 2g − 2 for all i, then q_d : Sht^d_B → Sht^d_H is smooth of relative dimension r/2 with fibres [G^{r/2}_a/Z]. Corollary 7.6: then the cone of Rπ^{<d}_{G,!}Q_ℓ → Rπ^{≤d}_{G,!}Q_ℓ is π^d_{H,!}Q_ℓ[−r](−r/2), a local system concentrated in degree r. Lemma 7.7 (Drinfeld, Varshavsky): p_{d,η} is finite and unramified on generic fibres, so the fundamental cycle of Sht^d_{B,η} defines the cohomological constant term γ_δ, and Lemma 7.8: γ_δ intertwines the H-action with the H_H-action through the Satake transform.
items.locator: §§7.2–7.3, Lemmas 7.4–7.5, 7.7–7.8, Corollary 7.6, pp. 849–857, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §7.4 (finiteness: Lemmas 7.9–7.13)
items.statement: With V = H^{2r}_c(Sht_G ⊗_k k̄, Q_ℓ)(r) filtered by L_{≤i}V coming from the truncations τ_{≤i}: Lemma 7.9: each L_{≤i}V is H-stable; Lemma 7.10: Gr^L_iV is finite dimensional for i ≠ r; Lemma 7.11: I_Eis·(L_{≤r}V) is finite dimensional; Lemma 7.13: V is a finitely generated H_x ⊗ Q_ℓ-module for every x ∈ |X|, and the image H_ℓ of H ⊗ Q_ℓ in End(V) is a finitely generated Q_ℓ-algebra of Krull dimension one.
items.locator: §7.4, Lemmas 7.9–7.13, pp. 857–865, published version
items.note: The authors note that this method should apply to moduli of shtukas for more general groups, giving information on their cohomology. Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Theorem 7.14, Lemma 7.15, Theorem 7.16 and Corollary 7.17 (the cohomological spectral decomposition)
items.statement: Theorem 7.14: (Spec H_ℓ)^{red} = Z_{Eis,Q_ℓ} ⊔ Z^r_{0,ℓ} with Z^r_{0,ℓ} a finite set of closed points, giving the decomposition of V; for r = 0 this reads Spec H^{red}_{aut,Q_ℓ} = Z_{Eis,Q_ℓ} ⊔ Z^0_{0,ℓ}. Lemma 7.15: H_aut ≅ Q[Pic_X(k)]^{ι_Pic} × H_cusp, i.e. Spec H_aut = Z_Eis ⊔ Z_cusp, and Z^0_{0,ℓ} = Z_{cusp,Q_ℓ}. Theorem 7.16 is the same statement for V′ on Sht′^r_G, and Corollary 7.17: the decomposition is orthogonal for the cup product, and I_r(f) = ([Sht_T]_Eis, f ∗ [Sht_T]_Eis) + Σ_{m ∈ Z′^r_{0,ℓ}(Q̄_ℓ)}I_r(m, f) with I_r(m, f) = ([Sht_T]_m, f ∗ [Sht_T]_m).
items.locator: §7.5, Theorem 7.14, Lemma 7.15, Theorem 7.16, Corollary 7.17, pp. 865–869, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Theorem 8.1 (the key identity for the Hecke functions h_D of large degree)
items.statement: For an effective divisor D on X of degree d ≥ max{2g′ − 1, 2g} and every u ∈ P¹(F) ∖ {1}, (log q)^{−r}J_r(u, h_D) = I_r(u, h_D); in particular (log q)^{−r}J_r(h_D) = I_r(h_D).
items.locator: Theorem 8.1, p. 869; proof in §8.3, pp. 874, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Propositions 8.2–8.3 and Corollary 8.4 (the direct image of f_M and the Hecke action on it)
items.statement: Proposition 8.2: for d ≥ 2g′ − 1 there is a canonical isomorphism of shifted perverse sheaves Rf_{M,*}Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i,j=0}^d (K_i ⊠ K_j)|_{A_d}, where K_i is built from the local systems L(ρ_i) on X̂_d attached to the double cover. Proposition 8.3: the action of f_{M,!}[H♦] preserves each summand and acts on K_i ⊠ K_j by the scalar (d − 2j). Corollary 8.4: hence I_r(u, h_D) = Σ_{i,j}(d − 2j)^rTr(Frob_a, (K_i)_a ⊗ (K_j)_a) when u = inv_D(a), and 0 otherwise.
items.locator: §8.1, Propositions 8.2–8.3, Corollary 8.4, pp. 869–872, published version
items.note: Proposition 8.3 is the computation that PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 reuses (its Proposition 11.7). Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.6 (the direct image of f_{N_d} and the matching of the two complexes)
items.statement: Proposition 8.5: for d ≥ 2g′ − 1 and d ∈ Σ_d, Rf_{N_d,*}L_d ≅ (K_{d_{11}} ⊠ K_{d_{12}})|_{A_d}, proved by showing that this complex is the middle extension from the open locus B = X_d ×_{Pic^d_X}X_d, using the smallness of the relevant maps and Verdier self-duality. Corollary 8.6: therefore Rf_{M,*}Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{d ∈ Σ_d}Rf_{N_d,*}L_d, matching the (i, j)-grading with the (d_{11}, d_{12})-grading — the perverse continuation principle that identifies the two sides.
items.locator: §8.2, Proposition 8.5, Corollary 8.6, pp. 872–874, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: Lemma 9.1, Theorem 9.2 and Corollary 9.4 (the key identity for all Hecke functions)
items.statement: Lemma 9.1: for any field E ⊇ Q, any nonzero ideal I of H_{x,E} and any m > 0, I + Span_E{h_{mx}, h_{(m+1)x}, …} = H_{x,E}. Theorem 9.2: (log q)^{−r}J_r(f) = I_r(f) for every f ∈ H, deduced from Theorem 8.1 by a density argument in the finitely generated algebra H̃_ℓ. Corollary 9.4: the action of H on W factors through H_aut, so W is a cyclic H_aut-module, finitely generated over each H_x.
items.locator: Lemma 9.1, Theorem 9.2, Corollary 9.4, pp. 874–879, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §9.1–9.3 (the proofs of Theorems 1.8, 1.6, 1.1 and 1.2)
items.statement: Theorem 1.8 follows from Theorem 9.2 with f = 1_K and Corollary 2.5 (§9.1.1). Theorem 1.6 follows by comparing the spectral decompositions: Σ_{m ∈ Z^r_{0,ℓ}}([Sht_T]_m, h ∗ [Sht_T]_m) = Σ_{π ∈ Z_cusp}(log q)^{−r}J_r(π, h) for h in a suitable ideal (§9.2). Theorem 1.1 follows from Corollary 9.4 and Lemma 7.15 (§9.3.1), and Theorem 1.2 from Theorem 1.6 and the compatibility of the intersection pairing with the cup product under the cycle class map (§9.3.2).
items.locator: §§9.1–9.3, pp. 874–879, published version
items.note: Routed to the Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), the candidate proposed by PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, whose brief already names this paper as the theory to plan it with.

items.name: §A.1 (rational Chow groups of proper cycles on Deligne–Mumford stacks)
items.statement: For a Deligne–Mumford stack X locally of finite type over k, Ch_{c,i}(X)_Q is the colimit of Ch_i(Y)_Q over closed substacks Y ⊆ X proper over k (§A.1.2); the degree map satisfies deg([x]) = [k_x : k]/|Aut(x)|_{k_x} (§A.1.3); for X smooth separated of pure dimension n the refined Gysin map along the diagonal gives the intersection product Ch_{c,i} × Ch_{c,j} → Ch_{c,i+j−n} and the pairing ⟨ , ⟩_X (A.1) (§A.1.4); the cycle class map cl_X : Ch_{c,j}(X)_Q → H^{2n−2j}_c(X ⊗_k k̄, Q_ℓ)(n−j) intertwines it with the cup product (§A.1.5); and cCh_n(X × X)_Q, the colimit over correspondences Z with proper first projection, is an associative Q-algebra acting on Ch_{c,i}(X)_Q (§A.1.6).
items.locator: §A.1, (A.1)–(A.2), pp. 880–882, published version
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: §A.2.1–A.2.7 (a filtration on K′_0 of a DM stack, Definition A.1 and Lemmas A.2–A.3)
items.statement: Definition A.1: a finite flat presentation of a DM stack X is a finite flat surjective map U → X from an algebraic space of finite type. §A.2.3 defines K′_0(X)_{Q,≤n} as the classes whose pullback to some finite flat presentation lies in the naive filtration — it can be nonzero for n < 0 (for X = BG it is the augmentation ideal of R_k(G)_Q). Lemma A.2: for algebraic spaces it agrees with the naive filtration. Lemma A.3: the filtration is preserved by finite flat representable pullback (and, §A.2.4, raised by d under flat maps of relative dimension d; §A.2.5, preserved by proper representable pushforward). §A.2.6 defines ψ_X : Gr_*K′_0(X)_Q → Ch_*(X)_Q by ψ_X(α) = (1/d)π_*ψ_U(π^*α) for a degree d presentation, and §A.2.7 shows it is compatible with the support map.
items.locator: §A.2.1–A.2.7, Definition A.1, Lemmas A.2–A.3, pp. 882–885, published version
items.note: Footnote 5 asks whether K′_0(X)_Q carries a natural λ-structure whose Adams eigenvalues would give the filtration. Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition A.5 and Corollary A.6 (refined Gysin maps versus Riemann–Roch)
items.statement: In a Cartesian square (A.3) in which X′ is a DM stack with a finite flat presentation and f factors as a regular local immersion of pure codimension e followed by a smooth morphism of relative DM type and pure relative dimension e − d (§A.2.8; Remark A.4: any morphism of smooth DM stacks factors this way), the derived pullback f^* sends K′_0(Y′)^{naive}_{Q,≤n} into K′_0(X′)_{Q,≤n−d} and the resulting square with the refined Gysin map f^! and the maps supp, ψ commutes (A.5); if Y′ also admits a finite flat presentation the same holds for the full filtration. Corollary A.6: for a smooth DM stack with a finite flat presentation, ψ_X is a graded ring homomorphism.
items.locator: §§A.2.8–A.2.9, Remark A.4, Proposition A.5, Corollary A.6, pp. 885–888, published version
items.note: The proof uses deformation to the normal cone for stacks and Fulton's Theorem 18.3(4). Corollary A.6 is not used in the paper. Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: §A.2.10, Remark A.7 and Lemma A.8 (the case of proper intersection)
items.statement: Under the alternative hypotheses of §A.2.10 — h (hence g) representable, the normal cone stack of f a vector bundle stack of constant virtual rank d, a smooth chart (A.8) by schemes in which the immersion is regular, and dim Y′ = n with dim X′ = n − d — the top-degree refined Gysin map f^! : Ch_n(Y′)_Q → Ch_{n−d}(X′)_Q is defined, and Lemma A.8: it is compatible with the derived pullback through the naive support maps, supp_{X′}∘f^* = f^!∘supp_{Y′}. Remark A.7: a morphism of smooth stacks always admits such a chart.
items.locator: §A.2.10, Remark A.7, Lemma A.8, pp. 889–890, published version
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: §A.3, Lemma A.9 and Theorem A.10 (the Octahedron Lemma)
items.statement: Given the 3×3 commutative diagram (A.10) of stacks with the fibre products of (A.11) and the stack N of (A.12), Lemma A.9 gives canonical isomorphisms (C ×_Y D) ×_{(U ×_S V)} (A ×_X B) ≅ N ≅ (C ×_U A) ×_{(Y ×_S X)} (D ×_V B). Theorem A.10: if (1) all of A, C, D, U, V, X, Y, S are smooth and equidimensional over k, (2) the four fibre products U ×_S V, Y ×_S X, C ×_Y D and C ×_U A have expected dimensions, (3) each of the squares (A.18) and (A.19) satisfies the conditions of §A.2.8 or of §A.2.10, and (4) the squares (A.13) and (A.14) satisfy the conditions of §A.2.8, then δ^!a^![B] = α^!d^![B] in Ch_n(N)_Q, where n = d_A + d_B + d_C + d_D − d_U − d_V − d_X − d_Y + d_S.
items.locator: §A.3, Lemma A.9, Theorem A.10, pp. 891–895, published version
items.note: "In calculating the intersection product of several cycles, one can combine terms and change the orders arbitrarily." The proof passes through a derived description of O_N, for which dg categories of coherent complexes are needed, and then through Proposition A.5 and Lemma A.8. Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: §A.4 (a Lefschetz trace formula for the intersection with the graph of Frobenius)
items.statement: For a self-correspondence C of M over S with cohomological correspondences ζ : ←c^*F → →c^!F, the pushforward h_! and the trace map τ_C : Hom(←c^*F, →c^!F) → H^{BM}_0(Fix(C) ⊗_k k̄) are those of Varshavsky. Lemma A.11: for M smooth separated of pure dimension n and F = Q_ℓ, the refined Gysin map Δ^!_M : Ch_n(C)_Q → Ch_0(Fix(C))_Q is compatible with τ_C through the cycle class maps. Proposition A.12: if moreover k is finite, S is a scheme, f : M → S is proper and ←c is representable and proper, then for every ζ ∈ Ch_n(C)_Q and every s ∈ S(k), ⟨ζ, Γ(Fr_M)⟩_s = Tr((f_!cl_C(ζ))_s ∘ Frob_s, (f_!Q_ℓ)_s), where the left side is the degree of the s-component of (id, Fr_M)^!ζ.
items.locator: §A.4, Lemma A.11, Proposition A.12, pp. 895–901, published version
items.note: The proof uses the excess intersection formula and Varshavsky's theorem that a contracting correspondence has naive local terms. Routed to EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.8 as a source.

items.name: §B.1 and Proposition B.1 (super-positivity for entire functions with RH)
items.statement: After recalling the Weierstrass product, genus, order and Hadamard's theorem g(φ) ≤ ρ(φ) ≤ g(φ) + 1: Proposition B.1. Let φ be entire with (1) φ(−s) = ±φ(s), (2) φ(s) ∈ R_{>0} for real s ≫ 0, (3) ρ(φ) ≤ 1, and (4) all zeros on the imaginary axis. Then φ^{(r)}(0) ≥ 0 for all r ≥ 0, and if φ is not constant, φ^{(r_0)}(0) ≠ 0 implies φ^{(r_0+2i)}(0) ≠ 0 for every i ≥ 0. The proof pairs the roots α ↔ −α = ᾱ and writes φ(s) = s^me^h∏_{i≥1}(1 + s²/(α_iᾱ_i)) with e^h > 0.
items.locator: §B.1, Proposition B.1, pp. 901–903, published version
items.note: Stark and Zagier obtained a similar result. Routed to AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem B.2, Lemma B.3 and Remarks B.4–B.7 (super-positivity of automorphic L-functions)
items.statement: For a nontrivial self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A) over a global field, with Λ(π, s) = N_π^{−(s−1/2)/2}L(π, s) and assuming the Riemann hypothesis for L(π, s) when F is a number field: (1) Λ^{(r)}(π, 1/2) ≥ 0 for all r ≥ 0; (2) if Λ is not constant, Λ^{(r_0)}(π, 1/2) ≠ 0 implies Λ^{(r_0+2i)}(π, 1/2) ≠ 0. Over a function field the hypothesis is a theorem (Deligne; Drinfeld and L. Lafforgue). Lemma B.3: if π_v is unitary and self-dual then L(π_v, s) has real coefficients, proved by showing L(π̄_v, s) = L(π̃_v, s) through the Godement–Jacquet local zeta integrals and complex conjugation of matrix coefficients. Remark B.4 gives an elementary function-field proof through the factorization λ(π, s) = (q^{s/2} − q^{−s/2})^a(q^{s/2} + q^{−s/2})^b∏_iA_i(s); Remarks B.5–B.7 record the cases known unconditionally (the Riemann zeta function; Sarnak's positive definite L-functions; Goldfeld–Huang; Lapid–Rallis for central values; Gross–Zagier and Yuan–Zhang–Zhang for first derivatives).
items.locator: §B.2, Theorem B.2, Lemma B.3, Remarks B.4–B.7, pp. 903–906, published version
items.note: Theorem B.2 is what makes Theorem 1.7 (positivity of the intersection pairing) unconditional over function fields. Routed to AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 as a source.

items.name: Bun_G, Bun_T and the adelic description of their points
items.statement: The moduli stacks Bun_G of G-bundles and Bun_T of T-bundles on X, their level structures, the identification Bun_G(k) ≅ G(F)\G(A)/K, and the exhaustion of Bun_G by finite-type open substacks by instability; also the Picard stacks Pic_X, Pic_{X′} and the Prym.
items.locator: §§1.1, 5.1, 5.4, 7.2, published version
items.note: GS.0 plans Bun_G with its level structures and Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, and the adelic description of rational points.

items.name: Perverse sheaves, middle extension, smallness and the decomposition theorem
items.statement: The middle perverse t-structure with intermediate extensions, the fact that the direct image of the constant sheaf under a small proper map is the middle extension from a dense open, Verdier self-duality up to twist for smooth sources, and the perverse continuation principle by which an isomorphism over a dense open extends.
items.locator: §§8.1–8.2 (Propositions 8.2, 8.5) and §6.2, published version
items.note: EDC.5 plans the perverse t-structure and intermediate extension, EDC.7 purity and the decomposition theorem.

items.name: Cohomological correspondences, trace maps and the Lefschetz–Verdier formalism
items.statement: Cohomological correspondences c_2^*K → c_1^!K with their composition and pushforward, the trace class in the Borel–Moore homology of the fixed-point stack, and the theorem that a contracting correspondence contributes naive local terms.
items.locator: §A.4.1–A.4.3, published version
items.note: EDC.8 plans cohomological correspondences, their composition and the trace class on the fixed-point scheme; §A.4 of this paper is the stacky Frobenius-graph refinement, routed as a source.

items.name: Chow groups of Artin stacks, refined Gysin maps and Riemann–Roch
items.statement: Chow groups of algebraic stacks with proper pushforward and flat pullback, refined Gysin maps for regular local immersions and for morphisms with vector bundle normal cone stacks, the excess intersection formula, deformation to the normal cone, and the Riemann–Roch map τ_X relating K-theory and Chow groups.
items.locator: §§A.1–A.2 (imported from Kresch, Fulton, Gillet, Vistoli), published version
items.note: SF.5 plans Chow groups, refined Gysin maps, intersection products and Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch; the extension to DM stacks with finite flat presentations, and the two new results of Appendix A, are routed as a source of that stage.

items.name: Everywhere unramified automorphic forms and the spherical Hecke algebra over a function field
items.statement: The space A = C^∞_c(G(F)\G(A)/K, Q) of everywhere unramified automorphic functions with its H-module structure, the decomposition into cuspidal, residual and Eisenstein parts, the coefficient field E_π = End_H(A_π) of an irreducible H-submodule, the Satake isomorphism and the Petersson inner product.
items.locator: §§1.2, 4.1–4.2, published version
items.note: FA.6 plans G(K)\G(A_K), compact-level functions, cuspidal subspaces, Hecke correspondences and the unramified Satake dictionary over a function field.

items.name: Standard and adjoint L-functions of automorphic representations over a function field, with the Riemann hypothesis
items.statement: For an everywhere unramified cuspidal π of PGL_2 over F: L(π, s) is a polynomial of degree 4(g−1) in q^{−s−1/2} with coefficients in O_{E_π}; the base change satisfies L(π_{F′}, s) = L(π, s)L(π ⊗ η_{F′/F}, s) with functional equation and epsilon factor ε(π_{F′}, s) = q^{−8(g−1)(s−1/2)}; the adjoint L-value L(π, Ad, 1); and the Riemann hypothesis for these L-functions, known over function fields by Deligne together with Drinfeld and L. Lafforgue.
items.locator: §1.2 and §B.2, pp. 769–770, 904, published version
items.note: AL.2 plans the Godement–Jacquet standard factors and FA.5 the function-field zeta and Artin factors with the Weil theorem; the global Langlands input for GL_n over function fields is cited by name only in the paper.

prerequisites.why: The original moduli of shtukas for GL_n; the r = 2 case of Theorem 5.4, and the source of Lemma 7.7 on the generic finiteness of p_d.

prerequisites.citation: Y. Varshavsky, Moduli spaces of principal F-bundles, Selecta Math. (N.S.) 10 (2004), no. 1, 131–166 [23]

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: special cycles on shtuka moduli and the higher Siegel–Weil formula
routes.reason: The objects are the moduli of PGL_2-shtukas with r legs, a finite cycle on it coming from a nonsplit torus, and the Chow/cohomology groups of that stack with their Hecke action: this is the direction of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, which owns Bun_G, the Hecke stacks, the shtuka stacks and their cohomology (GS.0–GS.7) but plans no cycles on them, no Hitchin-type comparison and no higher Gross–Zagier formula. It is deliberately the same Part II as the one PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 proposed: that paper's generalization to U(n) imports this paper's Octahedron Lemma and Hecke-action computation, and its brief already names this theory as the one to plan with it, so a second roadmap would duplicate the cycle theory. It is not GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights work: there is no height pairing and no Shimura variety here — the pairing is an intersection number of middle-dimensional cycles on a function-field moduli stack — although the r = 0 specialization, Waldspurger's formula, is routed to GZ.5 as a source, and GZ.5's number-field formula is what Remark 1.4 compares with.

GZ.5 plans the Waldspurger period formula for GL_2/quaternionic toric data, and asks for “the actual pairing identity including adjoint L-value, zeta/eta factors and normalized local toric forms” — but by the coherent theta-kernel route, importing Weil representations from MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–6. This source supplies the other proof, Jacquet's relative trace formula, in the everywhere unramified function-field case, where it is elementary and complete: the regularized distribution J(f, s) = ∫^{reg}_{[A]×[A]}K_f(h_1,h_2)|h_1h_2|^sη(h_2) with the finiteness theorems (Propositions 2.1 and 2.3) that make it a Laurent polynomial in q^s, its orbital expansion indexed by inv(γ) ∈ P¹(F) ∖ {1} with the explicit unramified computation J(u, 1_K, s) = L(η, 2s) + L(η, −2s) (Proposition 2.4), the Eisenstein ideal and the vanishing of the Eisenstein contribution to the kernel (Definition 4.1, Theorem 4.3), and the spectral expansion J_π(f, s) = (1/2|ω_X|)ℒ(π_{F′}, s + 1/2)λ_π(f) (Proposition 4.5, Theorem 4.7), which is Waldspurger's formula with exactly the adjoint L-value normalization GZ.5 requires (ℒ(π_{F′}, s) = ε(π_{F′}, s)^{−1/2}L(π_{F′}, s)/L(π, Ad, 1)). It also fixes the Whittaker/additive-character normalization (Lemma 4.6) that the eta and measure factors depend on. The higher-derivative content of the paper is not routed here: it is geometric and belongs to the Part II above.

SF.5 constructs Chow groups, proper pushforward, flat/lci pullback, refined Gysin maps, intersection products and source-scoped Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch. Appendix A of this paper is general intersection theory, with no shtukas in it, and adds four things SF.5 does not plan: (i) Chow groups Ch_{c,i}(X)_Q of cycles proper over k on a Deligne–Mumford stack only locally of finite type, with the degree map weighted by 1/|Aut|, the resulting intersection pairing on a smooth separated stack of pure dimension n, and the algebra cCh_n(X × X)_Q of correspondences with proper first projection acting on it; (ii) the corrected filtration K′_0(X)_{Q,≤n} defined through finite flat presentations (the naive filtration is wrong for stacks — for BG it misses the augmentation ideal, and the filtration can be nonzero in negative degrees), with the map ψ_X to Chow groups; (iii) Proposition A.5, that derived pullback along a morphism factoring as a regular local immersion followed by a smooth morphism of relative Deligne–Mumford type shifts this filtration by the relative dimension and commutes with the refined Gysin map through ψ, with the proper-intersection variant Lemma A.8 and Corollary A.6 (ψ_X is a graded ring homomorphism); and (iv) the **Octahedron Lemma** (Theorem A.10), which says that in a 3×3 diagram of smooth stacks with all four intermediate fibre products of expected dimension, two different orders of refined Gysin intersection give the same cycle class — the general form of “combine terms and change the orders arbitrarily” that both this paper and PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 use. Its proof needs a derived (dg) description of the structure sheaf of the central stack, which SF.5 should record as a hypothesis on its import rather than re-derive. Kresch, Fulton, Vistoli and Gillet, the sources SF.5 already builds on, are the prerequisites.

EDC.8 constructs cohomological correspondences c_2^*K → c_1^!K, their composition and the trace class on the fixed-point scheme, and states that ordinary Frobenius point counting stays with the trace formula stage. §A.4 supplies the case that a cycle-level theory needs and EDC.8 does not plan: for a self-correspondence C of a smooth separated stack M of pure dimension n over a base scheme S, with f proper and ←c representable and proper, the refined Gysin map Δ^!_M : Ch_n(C)_Q → Ch_0(Fix(C))_Q is compatible with Varshavsky's trace map τ_C through the cycle class maps (Lemma A.11), and the intersection number of a cycle with the graph of Frobenius computes a Frobenius trace on the stalk, ⟨ζ, Γ(Fr_M)⟩_s = Tr((f_!cl_C(ζ))_s ∘ Frob_s, (f_!Q_ℓ)_s) (Proposition A.12). This is the bridge from intersection numbers to trace formulas used in Theorems 6.5–6.6, and it is stated for Deligne–Mumford stacks, where the naive-local-term input is Varshavsky's contracting-correspondence theorem. Route it with the excess intersection formula of SF.5, which its proof consumes.

AL.2 constructs the Godement–Jacquet standard L-factors from local zeta integrals of matrix coefficients, proves the local functional equation and the unramified calculation, and builds the global integral for cuspidal GL_n with its Euler factorization, continuation and functional equation. Appendix B adds two results about those very objects that no stage in the atlas plans — nothing anywhere plans positivity of central values or of higher derivatives. First, Lemma B.3: if π_v is unitary then L(π_v, s) has real coefficients, because complex conjugation carries the space of matrix coefficients C_{π_v} to C_{σπ_v} and the Euler factor is determined by the space of zeta integrals — a statement about the AL.2 construction itself, using Godement–Jacquet Theorems 3.3 and 8.7. Second, Theorem B.2: for a nontrivial self-dual cuspidal π of GL_n(A), and assuming the Riemann hypothesis for L(π, s) when F is a number field, every derivative of the normalized completed L-function is non-negative, Λ^{(r)}(π, 1/2) ≥ 0, and the nonvanishing of one derivative forces that of all later ones of the same parity — “super-positivity”. It rests on the elementary Proposition B.1 about entire functions of order ≤ 1 with a functional equation and zeros on the imaginary axis, which belongs with the Hadamard factorization AL.2's global theory already needs; the trivial representation is handled by passing to s(s−1)Λ(π, s) (Remark B.5). Over a function field the hypothesis is a theorem, which is what makes Theorem 1.7 unconditional. Remark B.4's elementary function-field proof, through the factorization of λ(π, s) into (q^{s/2} ± q^{−s/2})-factors and the A_i(s) with positive even coefficients, belongs with FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5's polynomial zeta functions.
